name: The Twin Paradox
statement: A twin who travels at relativistic speed and returns has aged less than the twin who stayed on Earth, due to time dilation.
statementAccent: has aged less than the twin who stayed on Earth, due to time dilation
meaning: The twin paradox is a thought experiment illustrating that special relativity’s time dilation produces a real, asymmetric age difference between two observers, not merely an illusion. It appears paradoxical because each twin sees the other’s clock run slow, yet only one twin actually ages less.
mechanism: The apparent symmetry breaks because the travelling twin must accelerate to turn around, switching between different inertial reference frames, while the stay-at-home twin remains in a single inertial frame throughout. This asymmetry, combined with the relativity of simultaneity during the turnaround, resolves the paradox and predicts the correct, unequal elapsed proper times.

examples.text: Einstein’s original 1905 relativity paper noted that if one of two synchronised clocks is moved along a closed path and returned, it will lag behind the clock that stayed at rest.
Paul Langevin elaborated the scenario in 1911, describing a traveller moving at 99.995% of light speed who would age only about 2 years while roughly 200 years passed on Earth.

In the 1971 Hafele–Keating experiment, caesium atomic clocks flown around the world on airliners showed measurable time differences from a ground clock (about −59 ns eastward, +273 ns westward), directly confirming relativistic time dilation.

whyItMatters: The twin paradox is a key teaching tool for understanding that time dilation is a real, physically measurable effect rather than an optical or perceptual illusion, and it underlies practical corrections needed in technologies like GPS.
limits: As usually stated it is a special-relativistic scenario; a fully rigorous treatment of the accelerating twin’s frame requires careful use of instantaneous inertial frames or general relativity, and it does not by itself involve gravitational time dilation unless gravity is introduced.
misreadings: A common misreading is that the paradox represents a true logical contradiction in relativity; in fact it is resolved once the travelling twin’s non-inertial turnaround is properly accounted for.
origin: First discussed by Albert Einstein in his 1905 special relativity paper and developed into the named "twin" thought experiment by Paul Langevin in 1911.

sources.text: Twin paradox, Wikipedia. — the history from Einstein’s 1905 paper through Langevin’s 1911 formulation and the acceleration-based resolution.
